title: Signing out of cloud sync leaves local store intact; a subsequent sign-in on another account merges the previous user's data into the new account
detail: In js/core/cloud.js:114-126, signOut() sets session = null and revokes the Supabase token, but leaves KOS.store.state and all IndexedDB tables completely intact in localStorage and IndexedDB. When a second user signs in on the same browser (or the same user signs into a different account), cloudsync.js:pullRemote() runs mergeRemoteIn(local, remote) without account validation. The entire local database of user A (grades, money transactions, personal journal, habits, routines) is merged into user B's cloud storage and written permanently to Supabase.
repro:
1. Sign in as User A, log sessions and add transactions.
2. Sign out via Settings.
3. Sign in as User B.
4. Trigger cloud pull/sync.
5. Inspect User B's remote database in Supabase: User A's data has been uploaded and merged into User B.
rootCause: No account boundary or local data clearance policy on auth state transition; local persistence assumes single-user tenancy per device.
fix: On signOut(), prompt user to clear or retain local data; on sign-in with a different user ID, detect account mismatch (state.sync.lastUserId !== newUserId), refuse automatic merge, and offer clean slate or explicit migration.
whyMissed: QA audits only tested single-account syncing on test slots, never logging out and logging into a different account on the same browser profile.
openQuestions: Should local data wipe on sign-out be mandatory or optional with an export prompt?

title: Code runner: worker termination in kill() and sqlKill() abandons pending promises, permanently freezing the Run button
detail: In js/core/coderun.js:60-63 (kill()) and line 192 (sqlKill()), terminating the worker sets worker = null but does not reject or resolve pending promises in pending or sqlPending (unlike rtKill(), which properly iterates rtPending and settles with p.dead()). When a runtime error, memory limit, or worker crash occurs, the promise returned by KOS.coderun.run() hangs indefinitely, permanently locking the Run button in an unclickable disabled loading state.
repro:
1. Mount a Code task or SQL runner.
2. Dispatch a task that crashes the worker or triggers worker.onerror.
3. Observe the Run button state: spinner runs forever and never returns an error card.
rootCause: Asymmetry between rtKill() and kill()/sqlKill(); error handlers kill the worker process but orphan the pending promise registry.
fix: Mirror rtKill() in kill() and sqlKill(): iterate Object.keys(pending), clear watchdogs, delete entries, and resolve with an error result ({ ok: false, error: { code: 'CRASH', msg: 'Runner process terminated unexpectedly.' } }).
whyMissed: Audits tested normal execution and timeout watchdog expirations, but not uncaught worker process crashes or syntax errors during module initialization.
openQuestions: Does SQLite WASM emit a specific crash event before termination?

title: Achievement unlock dialog bypasses KOS.ui.openDialog, breaking modal stack, scroll lock, and trapping keyboard focus
detail: In js/core/achievements.js / js/modules/governor-ui.js, achievement unlock notifications render an overlay directly into document.body without invoking KOS.ui.openDialog(). It fails to register on dialogStack, does not set [data-scroll-lock], does not trap focus, and does not listen for Escape. When an achievement unlocks while a modal is already open (e.g. Afternoon Review, Preflight), the achievement dialog layers behind or between modals with no focus escape, causing a keyboard focus trap.
repro:
1. Open Afternoon Review dialog.
2. Trigger an achievement unlock condition.
3. Attempt to navigate via Tab or close with Escape.
rootCause: Invariant 13 violated: bypass of the unified KOS.ui.openDialog modal lifecycle for game-like popups.
fix: Route achievement celebrations through KOS.ui.openDialog() with appropriate stacking context and modal priority.
whyMissed: Achievement toasts were tested in isolation, not while another modal dialog was already open.
openQuestions: Should achievements queue behind active modal workflows until they close?

title: Theme showcase swatches and Shop department rail buttons lack accessible names, reading as unlabelled buttons
detail: In js/modules/governor-ui.js:840-880 and js/modules/governor-ui.js:920-940, theme swatch preview buttons and department icon buttons render without aria-label, title, or inner text, containing only inline styled <span> swatches. Screen readers announce bare 'button' with no indication of theme name or department, violating WCAG 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value.
repro:
1. Navigate to #cosmetics/shop with screen reader enabled.
2. Tab through the Theme showcase department.
3. Screen reader announces 'button' without color or theme name.
rootCause: Visual-only presentation without accessible name computation for graphical theme swatches.
fix: Add aria-label={theme.name + ' theme preview'} and title={theme.name} to every swatch button.
whyMissed: Visual and responsive audits checked render appearance but did not audit ARIA accessible names on swatch elements.

title: Daily Review evaluates morning window twice during autumn DST transition, re-prompting users after completion
detail: In js/modules/dayreview.js:45-55, date calculations assume standard 24-hour day durations when computing the 04:00 cutoff. On the night of autumn DST rollback (when local clock repeats 01:00-02:00), dayReview.shouldPrompt() evaluates true twice because the elapsed time check against last review completion evaluates the same calendar date with an earlier timestamp, prompting the user a second time.
repro:
1. Set system clock to DST fallback night at 01:30.
2. Complete Morning Review.
3. Advance clock past fallback to 01:30 again.
4. Launch KurenaiOS: Morning Review auto-opens again.
rootCause: Naive local date arithmetic without UTC timestamp anchoring or idempotent date-stamped completion flags.
fix: Key review completion by immutable ISO date string (completedDays[todayISO()] = true) rather than relative hour elapsed checks.
whyMissed: Harness slots run with static frozen timestamps and do not simulate time transitions across DST boundaries.
openQuestions: Are there other 04:00 routine resets affected by DST (e.g. streaks, habits)?

title: Multi-tab app version upgrades desynchronize store schema migrations, overwriting migrated state with stale memory cache
detail: In js/core/store.js:45-90, migrations run during boot when SCHEMA_VERSION increases. When two tabs are open during a service worker update: Tab 1 runs migrations and updates IndexedDB/localStorage. Tab 2 receives no storage event or reload signal; when Tab 2 later performs any user action, its unmigrated in-memory state object is serialized and saved via store.save(), overwriting Tab 1's migrated state and corrupting newly added schema fields.
repro:
1. Open two tabs of KurenaiOS on Version N.
2. Trigger an update in Tab 1 that migrates state.
3. In Tab 2, check a routine or add a note.
4. Reload Tab 1: migrated schema structures are overwritten with Tab 2's pre-migration layout.
rootCause: No BroadcastChannel or window.addEventListener('storage') synchronization between multiple tabs; in-memory state is treated as authoritative.
fix: Use a BroadcastChannel('kos_state') to signal state writes across tabs, or detect version changes in storage events and reload/rebaseline background tabs.
whyMissed: Test harness slots run single-page isolated browser contexts and do not test concurrent multi-tab persistence races.
openQuestions: Should Tab 2 immediately show a 'KurenaiOS has updated — reload to continue' banner?
